1	# local-whisper
2	
3	A fast, fully-local speech-to-text dictation tool for macOS with voice commands, powered by [whisper.cpp](https://github.com/ggml-org/whisper.cpp). No subscriptions, no cloud — just local transcription optimized for Apple Silicon.
4	
5	Hold **fn + left Control**, speak, release — text appears at your cursor.
6	
7	## Features
8	
9	- **Hold-to-dictate**: Hold the trigger combo to record, release to transcribe and insert
10	- **Segmented transcription**: Recordings are cut into 55-second segments and transcribed one after another, keeping each whisper call inside the model's sweet spot no matter how long you talk
11	- **Progress bar**: A two-colour strip shows recorded audio (red) against transcribed audio (blue), so long dictations report real progress
12	- **Voice commands**: Say "voice command note buy coffee" to save a note, "voice command open app Safari" to launch apps, and more — fully customizable
13	- **Recording indicator**: Pulsing red dot and elapsed timer in the overlay
14	- **Multi-language**: English, Russian, Ukrainian, and auto-detect (per segment, so mixed-language speech is not "translated")
15	- **App-aware processing**: Auto-capitalizes in most apps, skips in terminals and code editors
16	- **Text post-processing**: Remove filler words (um, uh, hmm), clean whitespace
17	- **Custom vocabulary / mixed-language anchor**: `~/.local-whisper/prompt` is a *writing sample*, not an instruction — whisper continues in whatever style it establishes. Seeded with a ru/uk/en example on first run; edit it to match how you actually speak. Applied to both the local model (with `--carry-initial-prompt`) and the remote API
18	- **Pipelined transcription**: Segments are transcribed while you are still talking, so the wait after releasing the key does not grow with the length of the dictation — only the tail segment is left. Text is inserted once all segments are back
19	- **Lossless capture**: A native AVAudioEngine recorder (`lw-record`) opens the microphone. ffmpeg's avfoundation input silently dropped ~10% of every recording, which swallowed whole words; the recorder logs captured-vs-wall-clock seconds after every dictation so a regression is visible
20	- **Warmup probe**: The recorder signals when audio is genuinely flowing; if the device never responds within 10 seconds, recording aborts with an error sound
21	- **Sleep recovery**: A dictation interrupted by system sleep is finalized on wake instead of being silently lost
22	- **Menu bar**: Waveform icon shows recording status (turns red), click for settings and recent dictations
23	- **Recent dictations**: View and re-paste your last 10 dictations from the menu bar
24	- **Fully local**: All processing on-device via whisper.cpp — nothing leaves your machine
25	
26	## Voice Commands
27	
28	Voice commands turn dictation into actions. All commands start with **"voice command"** to prevent false matches on normal speech.
29	
30	| Say | What happens |
31	|-----|-------------|
32	| "voice command note buy coffee" | Saves to `~/whisper_notes.md` |
33	| "voice command remind call mom" | Creates a Reminder in the Reminders app |
34	| "voice command open app Safari" | Launches or focuses an app |
35	| "voice command copy" | Fires Cmd+C |
36	| "voice command paste" | Fires Cmd+V |
37	| "voice command select all" | Fires Cmd+A |
38	| "voice command undo" | Fires Cmd+Z |
39	| "voice command cancel" | Discards the current dictation (works mid-sentence) |
40	
41	Voice commands are fully customizable — edit `~/.hammerspoon/local_whisper_actions.lua` to add your own. The config auto-reloads when you save.
42	
43	For a full guide on writing custom commands, see **[docs/VOICE_COMMANDS.md](docs/VOICE_COMMANDS.md)**.
44	
45	## Requirements
46	
47	- macOS (Apple Silicon recommended — tested on M4)
48	- [Homebrew](https://brew.sh)
49	
50	## Install
51	
52	```bash
53	git clone https://github.com/luisalima/local-whisper.git && cd local-whisper && ./install.sh
54	```
55	
56	The installer handles everything: Homebrew dependencies, building whisper.cpp, downloading models, and setting up Hammerspoon. It then runs `setup.sh` which walks you through choosing your trigger key, microphone, and granting permissions.
57	
58	To change the trigger key or re-run setup later:
59	
60	```bash
61	./setup.sh
62	```
63	
64	<details>
65	<summary>Manual install (if you prefer)</summary>
66	
67	```bash
68	# 1. Dependencies
69	brew install ffmpeg cmake git
70	brew install --cask hammerspoon
71	
72	# 2. Build whisper.cpp
73	cd ~
74	git clone https://github.com/ggml-org/whisper.cpp
75	cd whisper.cpp
76	cmake -B build
77	cmake --build build -j --config Release
78	
79	# 3. Download model (~1.5 GB)
80	./models/download-ggml-model.sh medium
81	
82	# 4. Copy Hammerspoon config
83	cp hammerspoon/init.lua ~/.hammerspoon/init.lua
84	```
85	
86	</details>
87	
88	## Uninstall
89	
90	```bash
91	./uninstall.sh
92	```
93	
94	Removes Hammerspoon config, `~/.local-whisper/` settings, and temp files. Optionally removes `~/whisper.cpp`. Does not uninstall Homebrew packages.
95	
96	## Setup
97	
98	### Permissions (System Settings > Privacy & Security)
99	
100	| App | Permission |
101	|-----|-----------|
102	| Hammerspoon | Accessibility, Microphone |
103	| Terminal (or your terminal app) | Accessibility (for `hs` CLI) |
104	
105	### Hammerspoon CLI
106	
107	Open Hammerspoon console and run once:
108	
109	```lua
110	hs.ipc.cliInstall()
111	```
112	
113	This installs the `hs` command-line tool used for IPC.
114	
115	### Audio device
116	
117	local-whisper records from your **macOS default input device**, so it follows your system
118	choice and survives dock/undock. To use a different microphone, change it in
119	**System Settings → Sound → Input**. There is no device setting in `init.lua`.
120	
121	## Menu bar
122	
123	A waveform icon in the menu bar shows recording status (turns red when recording). Click it to:
124	
125	- See current language, model, output mode, and enter mode
126	- Click any setting to cycle it
127	- View and re-paste recent dictations
128	- Reload voice commands
129	- Emergency stop
130	
131	All settings are accessible from the menu bar — no keyboard shortcuts needed.
132	
133	### Output modes
134	
135	Click **Output** in the menu bar to cycle through three modes:
136	
137	| Mode | Behaviour |
138	|------|-----------|
139	| **PASTE** | Writes text to clipboard via `pbcopy`, then sends `Cmd+V` automatically. Default for normal use. |
140	| **TYPE** | Types text character-by-character using keystroke events. Works in apps that block paste. Note: Cyrillic/non-ASCII may not work correctly in some apps. |
141	| **COPY** | Writes text to clipboard via `pbcopy` but does **not** send `Cmd+V`. Useful when working in **Microsoft Remote Desktop** or other remote-desktop/VM apps where clipboard sync to the guest OS is asynchronous — dictate, wait a moment for the clipboard to sync, then press `Ctrl+V` manually in the Windows window. |
142	
143	## Custom vocabulary prompt
144	
145	Create `~/.local-whisper/prompt` with terms whisper should recognize better:
146	
147	```
148	Claude, Hammerspoon, whisper.cpp, ffmpeg, macOS, Lua, Anthropic
149	```
150	
151	This text is passed as `--prompt` to whisper-cli for every segment of the recording. Adding your voice command trigger words here also improves recognition.
152	
153	## App-aware text processing
154	
155	Post-processing adapts to the frontmost application when you start recording:
156	
157	- **Terminals** (Terminal, iTerm2, Warp): skips auto-capitalize (commands are lowercase)
158	- **Code editors** (VS Code, Xcode, Zed, Sublime Text): skips auto-capitalize
159	- **Everything else**: auto-capitalizes first letter, removes filler words
160	
161	The active app is also available in voice command hooks as `ctx.appName` and `ctx.appBundleID`.
162	
163	## Writing custom voice commands
164	
165	Edit `~/.hammerspoon/local_whisper_actions.lua` to add your own commands. The file returns a table with hooks that run on each dictation:
166	
167	```lua
168	return {
169	    beforeInsert = function(ctx)
170	        -- Match and handle commands here
171	    end,
172	    actions = { },
